review_notes:
I read the whole file. It declares no @[simp] lemmas, no simp-set changes of its own, and no custom simp normal forms. The only simp-related content is the long `attribute [-simp]` and `attribute [-instance]` preamble and local `simp only` or `simp` calls.

The helper lemmas are `isUnit_iff_of_ringEquiv`, `mem_maximalIdeal_iff_of_ringEquiv`, `eval_map_symm` and `mem_nonunits_comap_iff`. I found no evidence that any of them needs a simp attribute. They are used by explicit `rw` or `exact` in the main theorem, and adding simp attributes to them would be speculative.

`isUnit_iff_of_ringEquiv` duplicates Mathlib's `MulEquiv.isUnit_map`, which is `@[simp high]` (Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Units/Equiv.lean). That is redundancy rather than a defect in the simp interface, so I did not report it.

The `simp at hm2` call in the third bullet is non-terminal and may be fragile. I did not report it because the rubric requires a concrete missing, misoriented or conflicting rule, and I could not run Lean to check.
